title: Commercial narrative for inference resilience
author: Leah Torres
body:
Overview

Purpose: This page provides a concise, repeatable commercial storyline and supporting artifacts for sales engineers and account executives pitching Redwood Inference to enterprise buyers where uptime, graceful degradation, regulatory constraints, and predictable economics matter. Use this as the single-place narrative to align technical risk reduction, pricing levers, and pilot -> production steps.

Audience: Sales engineers, solution architects, AE, technical program leads.

Problem statement

Enterprises building high-value features with LLMs face three correlated risks:
- Service disruption or degraded quality during peak load or model upgrades.
- Unpredictable unit economics from bursty usage and token-level pricing.
- Regulatory and data-control constraints that force private deployments.

Buyer's desired outcomes

1) Predictable availability and latency aligned to business SLAs (e.g., <100ms p95 for short completions, <500ms tail for contextual chat).
2) Clear cost controls and forecastability for the first 12 months of production.
3) Simple, auditable security posture for data-in-flight and at-rest.
4) Graduated rollback/fallback strategies to avoid feature outages during incidents.

High-level positioning / one-liners

- "Redwood Inference makes LLM features behave like mature, instrumented services: predictable latency, bounded cost, and auditable controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- Value drivers to emphasize: deterministic performance under load, production-grade fallbacks, and cost optimization tooling (batching, caching, quantization recommendations).

Competitive brief (short)

Cloud LLM endpoints (cloud hyperscalers)
- Strengths: deep infra footprint, integrated identity and billing.
- Risks for buyer: variable model performance across regions, limited model variants for graceful degradation, higher marginal costs for sustained token volumes.

LLM API providers (model-access-first)
- Strengths: broad model catalog, simple dev UX.
- Risks: less investment in autoscaling guarantees, limited on-prem options, few cost-optimization controls.

Self-hosted inference stacks / open-source runtimes
- Strengths: complete control, low marginal licensing.
- Risks: engineering ops burden, slower feature velocity, lack of standardized rollouts and observability.

How Redwood wins

- Unified runtime + orchestration: same SLO surface across hosted, Dedicated, and Private, reducing migration risk.
- Resilience primitives: automatic model fallbacks, per-customer routing policies, and KV/prefix caching that keep per-request latency bounded during degradation.
- Cost controls: pilot pricing constructs and Optimize recommendations that reduce unit economics risk.
- Security and compliance: customer-managed VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM KEs, and audit logs mapped to SOC2 evidence.

Pitch deck outline (one-slide per bullet)

1) Opportunity and buyer pain (quantified).
2) Redwood value proposition: predictable inference at scale.
3) Architecture diagram: client -> smart-routing -> runtime (cache, batching, quantized variants) -> fallback tiers.
4) Resilience features & runbook summary.
5) Pricing model and pilot-to-production roadmap.
6) Security posture and compliance artifacts.
7) Case study + ROI snapshot.
8) CTA: pilot proposal and technical onboarding timeline.

Executive-level ROI example (2-slide summary)

- Assumptions: 50M tokens/mo, peak 5k reqs/min, baseline provider price $0.0008/token.
- Redwood optimizations reduce effective unit token ops by 20% (caching/batching) and expected cost reduction by 28% vs baseline after quantization guidance.
- Example metric: expected monthly savings = (baseline - optimized) * tokens = ~$11.2k/mo. (Detailed numbers are illustrative; run pricing simulator per account.)

Pilot structure (recommended commercial + technical milestones)

1) 6-week technical pilot (free or deeply discounted compute + capped usage):
   - Week 0: kickoff, NDA, security questionnaire review.
   - Week 1: sample integration (API keys, VPC peering for Private pilots).
   - Week 2–3: workload profiling, sequence length distribution capture, and initial model variant selection.
   - Week 4: enable caching/continuous batching; run cost baseline.
   - Week 5: resilience test (failover exercise + region failback).
   - Week 6: pilot review, recommended rollout plan, and commercial ask.

2) Commercial ask: 3-month reserved capacity trial with optional commitment discount and uplift to Dedicated. Include a rollback SLA and a pre-agreed A/B test for quality.

Pricing guidance (simple templates for negotiation)

- Pilot pricing: compute credits + consult time (flat fee) with a capped usage threshold (e.g., 100M tokens) charged at pilot rate $0.0003/token beyond cap.
- Transition to production: tiered reserved capacity with commit bands (monthly): 0–500M tokens, 500M–2B, >2B. Offer 10–25% discounts for 12-month commits.
- Add-on: extended observability retention and compliance package (flat monthly fee).

Sample pricing matrix (text-table)

| Tier | Monthly commit | Effective token rate (est) | Notes |
| ---- | -------------- | ------------------------- | ----- |
| A - Pilot | 0–0.5B | $0.00045 | short-term trial pricing, includes onboarding hours |
| B - Standard | 0.5B–2B | $0.00030 | reserved capacity, standard SLA |
| C - Enterprise | >2B | $0.00022 | higher commit, dedicated scaling, prioritized support |

Negotiation levers to protect margins

- Limit free compute credits and attach professional services hours for heavy customization.
- Tie deeper discounts to committed throughput and minimum contract length.
- Keep chargeable extras explicit: model onboarding, private deployment brokerages, extended data retention.

Case study (compact)

Customer: FinSecure (an enterprise financial platform)
Problem: Inconsistent latency across regions and unpredictable month-to-month inference spend during events.
Outcome after 6 months: Achieved 99.95% uptime for inference APIs, reduced per-token cost by 32% through caching and batch tuning, and completed an on-prem Private deployment with audited KMS keys. Business impact: enabled real-time fraud alerts with <200ms p95 and avoided $275k in incremental cloud spend over 6 months.

Security FAQ (for prospect-facing conversations)

Q: Can you run in our VPC/on-prem?
A: Yes. Redwood offers Private deployments (VPC and on-prem packaging). We support customer-managed control planes and HSM/KMS integrations. See deployment checklist below.

Q: How is data partitioned between customers?
A: Multi-tenancy is logically isolated per-customer. Dedicated pools optionally provide physical GPU isolation. Session-level metadata and KV caches are segmented per-tenant.

Q: What monitoring & audit evidence do you provide?
A: Token-level billing exports, model and route-level latency histograms, per-request traces (sampling), and immutable audit logs for administrative actions. We provide SOC2 evidence packages and can assist in third-party audits.

Q: How do you ensure rollback and graceful degradation?
A: Automatic fallbacks to lower-cost/quantized model variants, region rerouting policies, and an A/B rollback policy that can be triggered by error rate or quality regression thresholds. We run scheduled canaries and automated health checks.

Deployment checklist (table)

| Item | Owner | Target | Compliance artifact |
| ---- | ----- | ------ | ----------------- |
| Network connectivity (VPC peering, GW) | Customer/Redwood | 1 week | Network diagrams, peering logs |
| Key management (KMS/HSM) | Customer | 2 days | KMS key policy export |
| Data retention policy and SIEM integration | Customer | 2 weeks | Retention table, SIEM ingest config |
| SLA acceptance tests | Redwood/Customer | 1 week | Test runbook + results |

Actionable playbook snippets

- Enabling a fallback policy (CLI example):

redwoodctl rollout create --name "canary-fallback-1" --model-group prod-gptx --fallback-to quantized-gptx-q4 --trigger-error-rate 0.01 --rollout-percent 10

- Simplified JSON response for billing export (sample):
{
  "customer_id": "cust-123",
  "month": "2026-02",
  "tokens": "51234567",
  "cost_usd": "14602.34"
}

Objections and rebuttals (short)

- "We can self-host cheaper." -> Rebuttal: Self-hosting trades capex for ops risk; Redwood's Optimize and routing policies reduce operational cost and support faster incident recovery.
- "We need ironclad SLAs." -> Rebuttal: Redwood provides Dedicated pools with SLA-backed latency and uptime targets plus documented escalation runbooks.

Next steps (templated CTA)

1) Propose a 6-week pilot scope + commercial term template.
2) Schedule a resilience tabletop exercise with SRE and product stakeholders.
3) Provide tailored ROI spreadsheet and a reserved-capacity term sheet.

Appendix: Suggested SLOs and alert thresholds

- P95 latency (short completions): 100ms target, 150ms warning, 250ms critical.
- Error rate (5xx): 0.1% target, 0.5% warning, 1% critical.
- KV cache hit rate: >60% target for chat workloads.

Document maintenance

Owner: go-to-market. Update cadence: quarterly or after major runtime/resilience feature releases.
